guideTitle: 6 Best Wood Pellet Patio Heaters in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Wood Pellet Patio Heaters in 2026
metaDescription: Six wood pellet patio heaters compared on hopper size, burn time, tower height, rain caps, wheels and heat claims for ambiance and gentle outdoor warmth.
introParagraphs: Wood pellet patio heaters are part heater, part fire feature. A vertical tube burns small wood pellets with a tall, swirling flame, so you get firelight and some warmth without the logs, sparks and heavy smoke of a campfire. They are not as strong as a propane tower, and most makers describe the warmth as gentle and localized, so they suit cool evenings and ambiance more than serious cold-weather heating.

This lineup covers six pellet heaters. The NUUK claims 70,000 BTU with a gravity feeding system, the GARDENFLARE 58 inch premium holds 4.5 pounds for up to 90 minutes, the COWVIE holds about 5 pounds for 90 to 120 minutes, the JIAYAN adds lockable wheels and a stainless rain cap, the YTGLEN stands 64.47 inches with a 4.4 pound hopper, and the Rayzi 55 inch holds 2.2 pounds for about 75 minutes. Burn times are the maker's claims for one fill.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on hopper size, burn time, build and cleanup. These are fuel-burning outdoor heaters, so keep them well away from flammables and never use them in an enclosed space.

products.name: NUUK 70,000 BTU Wood Pellet Patio Heater
products.description:
The NUUK is the only pellet heater here that leads with a heat figure, claiming up to 70,000 BTU for patios, decks, backyards and gathering spaces. A gravity feeding system supplies a steady, natural-looking flame, and a built-in glass viewing window shows the glow. The listing adds that a brief amount of visible smoke may appear on startup while the fire and chimney warm up.

The gravity feed means you do not tend the fire constantly, which is a real convenience over simpler fire tubes. Wheels are built in, so you can reposition it where warmth is needed. The BTU claim is the highest in the group and the most useful comparison point against propane units. The tradeoff is that a stated BTU does not guarantee comfort, since distance, wind and reflector design all change what you feel, and the listing gives no hopper size or burn time.

For ownership, expect to clear ash, keep pellets dry and let the startup smoke clear before guests sit close. Compared with the GARDENFLARE Premium at 4.5 pounds and 90 minutes, it makes a stronger heat claim but offers far fewer practical specs. Compared with the Rayzi 55 inch at 2.2 pounds, it is aimed at heating rather than decoration. It suits buyers who want a pellet unit that reads as a real heater.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a pellet unit with a stated heat output and steady feed.
pros: Up to 70,000 BTU heat claim
Gravity feeding keeps flame steady
Glass viewing window and built-in wheels
Natural wood pellet flame
cons: Hopper size and burn time not stated

products.name: GARDENFLARE Premium 58 Inch Wood Pellet Patio Heater
products.description:
The GARDENFLARE Premium is a 58 inch fire tube that the listing says gives 81 percent more flame volume than the maker's Classic. It promises a flame up to 5 feet tall and up to 90 minutes per fill, with a 44 inch borosilicate glass tube. It burns standard softwood pellets from a 4.5 pound capacity with very little smoke.

The frame is heavy-duty stainless steel with a matte black powder-coated finish, and setup takes 5 to 10 minutes with the included Allen key. Documented hopper size and burn time make planning easy, which most rivals do not offer. The larger flame brings more visual impact and more radiant warmth than the smaller Classic. The tradeoff is that no BTU figure is given, so it is best treated as an ambiance feature with some warmth.

For ownership, a 90 minute fill means a refill during a long dinner, and the ash needs clearing once the unit cools. Controlled airflow keeps the burn even, but pellets must stay dry for it to work well. Compared with the COWVIE at about 5 pounds and 90 to 120 minutes, it burns slightly less per fill but documents its flame height. Compared with the NUUK, it trades a big BTU claim for clearer practical specs.
products.bestFor: Entertaining spaces that want a tall flame and clear fuel specs.
pros: 4.5 pound capacity with up to 90 minute burn
Up to 5 foot flame in a 44 inch glass tube
Stainless steel frame with powder coat
Tool-light setup in 5 to 10 minutes
cons: Needs a refill during long evenings

products.name: COWVIE 56 Inch Patio Wood Pellet Heater With Rain Cap
specs: About 5 lb per load, 90 to 120 minutes
products.description:
The COWVIE is a 56 inch pellet heater that burns 6mm hardwood pellets for a low-smoke flame. A full load of about 5 pounds is claimed to give 90 to 120 minutes of gentle, localized warmth. The metal body has a heat-resistant black finish, a rain cap and an integrated pellet viewing window.

A reinforced square steel base keeps it steady on lawns, soil and decks, and the viewing window lets you check pellet level without lifting anything. The listing frames the warmth as taking the chill off a seating area rather than heating a yard. The removable ash tray and an included sponge cleaning rod help keep the glass tube clear. The tradeoff is that there is no BTU rating, so heat expectations should stay modest.

For ownership, wait until the unit is cool before emptying ash and use the rod to wipe soot from the tube. Keep pellets dry and store the rain cap fitted. Compared with the GARDENFLARE Premium at 4.5 pounds and up to 90 minutes, it holds more and burns longer per fill. Compared with the YTGLEN at 4.4 pounds and about 2 hours, it burns a bit shorter but adds a rain cap.
products.bestFor: Cool evenings where gentle warmth and a long burn per fill matter.
pros: 90 to 120 minutes per 5 pound load
Rain cap and pellet viewing window
Reinforced square steel base
Includes sponge rod for the glass tube

products.name: JIAYAN 64 Inch Wood Pellet Patio Heater With Wheels
specs: Lockable caster wheels and carry handle

specList.label: Cleanup
specList.value: Detachable ash tray and air inlet

products.description:
The JIAYAN is a 64 inch pellet patio heater with lockable caster wheels and a built-in carry handle. A stainless steel rain cap resists rust and blackening and keeps burning steady in light rain or mist. Spiral flames rise inside a 3.14 inch wide glass tube, and an adjustable air inlet controls flame size and efficiency.

The detachable ash tray collects residue for quick cleanup, and the wheels let you move it when fully cooled and then lock it in place. The listing recommends 6mm pine pellets and warns that oversized pellets can blacken the glass tube. Lighting uses a fire starter or alcohol block at the base, and the flame reaches its best state in about 10 minutes. The tradeoff is that hopper size and burn time are not stated, so you cannot plan refills.

For ownership, open the discharge port to unload unused pellets when you are done, and keep the area ventilated while residual flames go out in 10 to 15 minutes. Wheels need level ground, since a tall tube on a slope is a tipping risk. Compared with the COWVIE at 56 inches, it is taller and far easier to move. Compared with the YTGLEN at 64.47 inches, it documents mobility and cleanup where the YTGLEN is mostly silent.
products.bestFor: Patios where the heater gets moved and cleanup should be easy.
pros: Lockable wheels and carry handle
Stainless steel rain cap resists rust
Detachable ash tray for cleanup
Adjustable air inlet controls flame size
cons: Hopper size and burn time not stated

products.name: YTGLEN 64 Inch Wood Pellet Patio Heater With Glass Tube
products.description:
The YTGLEN is a 64 inch tower that stands 64.47 inches tall and puts the flame at eye level for seated guests. It holds up to 4.4 pounds of wood pellets for approximately 2 hours of continuous burning, depending on fuel and conditions. A glass tube shows the vertical flame from several viewing angles around the unit.

The body is heavy-duty iron with a weather-resistant finish, a sturdy base and a removable ash tray. It is the longest burn per fill in this group among units with a stated capacity. The listing says it is for wood pellets only and for outdoor use, with a safe distance from children, pets and combustible materials. The tradeoff is that there is no BTU rating and no mention of wheels, a rain cap or a viewing window for fuel level.

For ownership, plan to let it cool completely before emptying the ash tray and keep the area clear of anything flammable. Because there is no wheel kit, think of it as a fixed feature once it is placed. Compared with the Rayzi at 2.2 pounds and over 75 minutes, it nearly doubles the burn time. Compared with the COWVIE at about 5 pounds, it holds slightly less but offers a longer claimed run of about 2 hours.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a long burn per fill and a glass flame display.
pros: About 2 hour burn on 4.4 pounds
64.47 inch tower puts flame at eye level
Heavy-duty iron with removable ash tray
Glass tube visible from multiple angles
cons: No wheels or rain cap listed

products.name: Rayzi 55 Inch Decorative Wood Pellet Heater
products.description:
The Rayzi 55 inch is a rocket-style pellet stove with a 1000mm long, 80mm wide glass tube and a spiral flame. Its 2.2 pound hopper gives a flame lasting over 75 minutes, and the listing cites up to 3.6 kilowatts of flame intensity. The base is high-temperature resistant carbon steel.

The listing is unusually honest that the product is primarily intended for admiration and ambiance, with relatively limited heating functionality. A removable ash tray captures the small amount of residue, and a fire starter and lighter light it. The tradeoff is the compact hopper, which means refilling during a long evening, and the modest heat that comes with it. It is the entry point for people who mainly want the flame.

For ownership, keep the filler cap closed while lighting to limit smoke, and pull the ash box out slightly if the first flame burns slowly. Pellets must stay dry, and ash should only be emptied once everything is cool. Compared with the GARDENFLARE Premium at 4.5 pounds and up to 90 minutes, it holds half as much fuel. Compared with the YTGLEN at 4.4 pounds, it burns about 45 minutes less per fill.
products.bestFor: Short evenings and small gatherings where look matters most.
pros: Spiral flame in a 1000mm glass tube
Over 75 minutes on a 2.2 pound hopper
Removable ash tray for easy cleanup
High-temperature carbon steel base

buyingCriteria.explanation: Pellet heaters give gentle, localized warmth, and some makers say so outright. The Rayzi listing calls its heating functionality limited, while the NUUK claims up to 70,000 BTU and most others state no figure. Rated BTU alone does not predict comfort, because distance, wind and tube design all change what you feel. A good rule is to sit within a few feet and treat the unit as a way to take the chill off. For serious cold, a propane tower or infrared unit is a better tool.

Fuel capacity sets how often you refill during an evening. The Rayzi holds 2.2 pounds for over 75 minutes, the GARDENFLARE Premium holds 4.5 pounds for up to 90 minutes, the COWVIE holds about 5 pounds for 90 to 120 minutes, and the YTGLEN holds 4.4 pounds for about 2 hours. Choose a larger hopper if you host dinners that last longer than an hour. Remember that burn time is the maker's claim for one fill under ideal conditions.

Pellets burn cleaner than logs, but not smokelessly. The COWVIE uses 6mm hardwood pellets, the JIAYAN recommends 6mm pine pellets, and the GARDENFLARE burns standard softwood pellets with very little smoke. The NUUK notes a brief amount of visible smoke on startup. Oversized pellets can blacken the glass tube, so use the size the maker lists and keep them dry.

A rain cap keeps weather out of the tube so the burn stays steady. The COWVIE has a rain cap and a reinforced square steel base, and the JIAYAN has a stainless steel cap that resists rust and blackening. These towers are tall and narrow, so base design matters, and the JIAYAN's wheels need to be locked on level ground. Never place one on a slope or a wobbly deck board.

Ash is part of ownership with any pellet unit. The JIAYAN has lockable caster wheels, a carry handle and a detachable ash tray, while the COWVIE and Rayzi have removable ash trays. The NUUK has built-in wheels but documents little else about cleaning. Let the unit cool fully before moving it or emptying ash. A cleaning rod such as the one with the COWVIE keeps the glass tube clear.

These are fuel-burning outdoor heaters, and the YTGLEN listing says to keep a safe distance from children, pets and combustible materials. Keep every unit away from awnings, overhanging branches, low pergolas and fabric, and never use one in a garage, tent or enclosed porch. The 64 inch JIAYAN and YTGLEN and the 58 inch GARDENFLARE need real headroom overhead. Place them on a noncombustible, level surface.

faq.a: They give gentle, localized warmth, enough to take the chill off a seating group. The NUUK claims up to 70,000 BTU, but most others state no figure, and the Rayzi listing calls heating limited. They do not match propane towers for warming a whole patio. Sit close and treat them as an ambiance feature with some heat.

faq.q: How long does one fill last?
faq.a: The Rayzi lasts over 75 minutes on 2.2 pounds, the GARDENFLARE Premium up to 90 minutes on 4.5 pounds, the COWVIE 90 to 120 minutes on about 5 pounds, and the YTGLEN about 2 hours on 4.4 pounds. These are the makers' claims for one fill. Cold and wind shorten the burn, so keep extra pellets nearby.

They burn cleaner than logs, but none is truly smokeless. The COWVIE and GARDENFLARE describe low smoke, and the NUUK notes brief visible smoke while it warms up. Smoke increases with damp pellets or oversized pellets. Keep the filler cap closed while lighting to limit smoke.

faq.q: Can I use one indoors or on a covered porch?
faq.a: No. These are fuel-burning heaters and are for outdoor use only because of carbon monoxide and fire risk. Keep them clear of flammables, awnings and low ceilings, and follow the manual's distances. A well-ventilated open area is the only safe setting.

faq.q: How do I clean a pellet heater?
faq.a: Let it cool completely, then empty the ash tray and wipe the glass tube. The JIAYAN has a detachable ash tray and an unloading port for unused pellets, and the COWVIE includes a sponge cleaning rod. Keep pellets dry between uses. Dispose of ash only when it is fully cold.

Use the type and size the maker lists. The COWVIE uses 6mm hardwood pellets, the JIAYAN recommends 6mm pine pellets, and the GARDENFLARE burns standard softwood pellets. Oversized pellets can blacken the glass, and other fuels are not safe. Store pellets in a dry container.

faq.q: Which one is easiest to move around?
faq.a: The JIAYAN has lockable caster wheels and a carry handle, and the NUUK has built-in wheels. Always move a unit only when it has fully cooled. Lock the wheels on level ground before lighting it, since a tall glass tube is a tipping risk.
